A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Diffusion Probe study. The complete main texts, equations, seven tables, ten figures, and supplementary sections are readable and support comparison despite repagination.

before.justification: v1 reports original predictive-accuracy experiments, downstream generation comparisons, Flow-GRPO training results, and appendix ablations, robustness analyses, and human-alignment results.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results in Sections 4–5, Tables 1–7, and the main and supplementary figures.

M1.justification: Sections 3.3–3.4 retain the same attention-map CNN, timestep input, scalar quality prediction, MSE objective, and procedures for prompt optimization, seed selection, and Flow-GRPO. No method component is added or revised.

E1.justification: Both versions use MS-COCO 2017 prompts for the same quality-prediction and downstream tasks, retaining the appendix prompt-complexity and human-alignment evaluations. Newly mentioned applications such as object removal and virtual try-on are background citations, not new evaluations.

E2.justification: The baseline and LLM comparisons in Table 2, random-seed baseline, original Flow-GRPO comparator in Figure 5, and brute-force workflows in Table 3 are unchanged. Newly cited methods do not enter these comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains 15,000 training and 5,000 test prompts, 25 generation steps, default extraction at step 5, ten seed candidates, and four prompt variants. Appendix sampling settings and Section 6.1's score-selection and median-threshold AUC procedures also match.

E4.justification: The timestep, resolution, and supervision-metric studies in Tables 1, 4, and 5 are retained. Appendix architectural, prompt-complexity, attention-feature, diversity, and failure-mode analyses were already present in v1 and remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version introduces repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance testing. The seed-selection pool, point-estimate reporting, training curves, and PickScore-variance discussion are unchanged.

E6.justification: All seven tables retain their numerical entries: for example, FLUX at step 10 remains SRCC 0.79 and AUC 0.91 in Table 1, and probe-guided seed-selection latency remains 42.62 seconds in Table 3. Figure 5's curves, appendix findings, and qualitative examples and scores also match.

T1.justification: The mathematical descriptions of diffusion and MM-DiT, quality-prediction mapping, MSE loss, threshold-based prompt refinement, and argmax seed selection are unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical assumptions, propositions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and numbered contributions retain the same claims about early attention predicting final quality, a lightweight model-agnostic probe, and benefits for three downstream applications. The shortened conclusion preserves these claims.

C2.justification: Both retain the same interpretations linking attention dispersion to generation failures, robustness to noise-level features, and filtering to training efficiency and preserved diversity. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added.

D1.justification: v5 adds a code-availability statement and repository link in the abstract, absent from v1. Implementation settings, hardware, processing details, and runtime information otherwise remain unchanged. The PDFs establish the new access information, not the repository's contents.

R1.justification: The bibliography expands from 30 to 40 works. Two brief background passages in Section 2 and appendix Section 5 add context on diffusion applications and multimodal intelligence, citing works including TC-Padé, ShoeFit, Yuvion VL, and GUIDE. The central research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 4.5 is rewritten more concisely, two short background passages are added, and affiliation, email, and corresponding-author details are edited. Section ordering and almost all methodological and experimental prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v5 adds branded headers and page numbers, tightens spacing around displays, and uses smaller reference typography to consolidate the bibliography. The ten scientific figures and seven tables retain their content and organization, with placement shifts caused by reflow.

improvement.justification: The newly documented code location and more concise conclusion provide limited improvements in reproducibility information and readability. Scientific methods and evidence remain unchanged. The added background offers modest context, while smaller bibliography text reduces legibility, keeping the overall benefit limited.
